description:
Five months after the conflict with Iran began, the United States faces a difficult question: how does it end a war that has failed to produce a decisive outcome? 
President Trump has alternated between threatening overwhelming force and signaling diplomacy, but Tehran continues to resist U.S. demands while leveraging disruption in the Strait of Hormuz to strengthen its negotiating position.

This discussion examines Trump's military, diplomatic and political options, Iran's strategy of endurance, and whether either side has a realistic path toward ending one of the most consequential geopolitical crises of 2026.

description:
Hundreds of migrants remain in Ceuta waiting to find out what happens next, with many camping on the beaches and their future in the hands of authorities. Twenty-nine-year-old Ahmed Haroun, originally from Sudan's Darfur region, is one of them. He said he has been trying to reach Europe for four years to help his surviving family members, having lost many relatives already. "I will fight for them. I will do anything just to help them," he said. He said he had achieved his dream by reaching Ceuta and is not afraid of being deported. "Everyone here just died one time. No one can die two times," he said. He expressed hope for a humanitarian response, saying they are waiting to hear what authorities will decide.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Iran and Oman are making progress in talks over arranging the passage of vessels through the Strait of Hormuz, with discussions focused on technical and political issues, although no final agreement has been reached.
A proposed framework under discussion would give Iran control over inbound shipping, while Oman would clear outbound vessels after notifying Tehran.
Iranian officials insist the talks are only bilateral between Tehran and Muscat, with Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei blaming the United States for the crisis at the strait.
Washington, however, says there has been progress, with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio acknowledging movement in talks and the Treasury Department pointing to an opportunity to reopen the waterway.
Maritime risks remain high, with vessels continuing to face projectile attacks despite diplomatic efforts.
As rhetoric remains tense on both sides, the Strait of Hormuz continues to be Iran’s main source of strategic leverage.

Al Jazeera’s Mah
title: Iran-Oman Hormuz talks progress, US acknowledges advance
